argument: I support this DOW short from an Asia macro perspective, particularly regarding Japanese industrial demand patterns and China spillover effects. From my Japan coverage, I'm seeing several reinforcing factors: 1) Japan's industrial production has been volatile, with machinery orders showing weakness - this directly impacts chemical intermediates demand that DOW supplies to Japanese manufacturers. 2) The China construction slowdown thesis is critical - Japan's chemical exports to China have been declining as Beijing's property sector remains depressed, hitting polyethylene and packaging demand. 3) USD/JPY dynamics amplify the problem: at current levels (~155), Japanese importers face higher dollar costs for commodity chemicals, reducing volume demand and pushing them toward domestic alternatives or demand destruction. 4) Most importantly, Japan's manufacturing PMI has been hovering around 50, indicating flat industrial activity. When Japanese auto and electronics production is soft, it reduces demand for Dow's upstream chemical inputs. 5) The technical data showing DOW underperforming XLB by -26.2% over 63 days aligns with what I'm seeing in Asia - commodity chemicals are getting hit harder than specialty materials in this cycle. The upcoming ISM Manufacturing PMI (Aug 3) and any Japan industrial production data will likely confirm continued weakness in the industrial chemical cycle that underpins this short thesis.
